---
title: "The q2 language server"
description: "What `q2 lsp` offers editors and developer tooling: project-aware diagnostics and outlines, and the `quarto/documentMetadata` and `quarto/documentProfile` protocol extensions for a document's merged metadata and Pass-1 profile."
---

## Overview

`q2 lsp` runs a [Language Server
Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/) server over
stdio. Editors use it for diagnostics and the document outline. Developer
tooling can also use it to ask about a document: its merged metadata and its
*profile*, the summary Quarto computes before rendering (title, authors,
outline, comments, includes, links).

The server analyses every document **inside its project**. It reads
`_quarto.yml` and the `_metadata.yml` files that apply, picks the format
`q2 render` would use, and follows `{{{< include >}}}` shortcodes. It analyses
the text in the editor, including unsaved edits. An unsaved edit to an included
file or to `_metadata.yml` updates the documents that depend on it.

```bash
q2 lsp
```

## Initialization options

Pass these as `initializationOptions` in the `initialize` request:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `profile` | Active [project profiles](../guides/projects/profiles.qmd): a string or a list of strings. Defaults to `QUARTO_PROFILE`. |
| `sweep` | When a project is opened, profile all of its documents in the background (default `true`). Set it to `false` for very large workspaces. |

## Standard features

- `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` reports parse, metadata, include and
  language diagnostics for each open `.qmd` and `.md` document.
- `textDocument/documentSymbol` returns the outline: headings, code cells
  and cross-reference targets, numbered as in the rendered document.

An open `_quarto.yml` or `_metadata.yml` counts for the documents that read
it, but the server does not analyse it as a document.

## Protocol extensions

The server advertises its extensions in `ServerCapabilities.experimental`.
Each entry gives a method's schema version, and clients should check it
before calling:

```json
{ "experimental": { "quarto": { "documentMetadata": 1, "documentProfile": 1 } } }
```

Both methods accept the URI of any `.qmd` or `.md` file, whether or not it is
open. For an open document the answer reflects the buffer, and `version` is
its version. Otherwise the server reads the file, and `version` is `null`.
Both methods take an optional `format`. When it is omitted, the server uses
the document's own format, the one `q2 render` would pick.

### `quarto/documentMetadata`

Returns the document's **merged metadata**. That is the project config,
`_metadata.yml` layers, front matter and `format.<name>` options, combined as
a render combines them. It is the same value `q2 get-config` prints. Tools
should use it instead of reimplementing how those layers combine.

```jsonc
// params
{
  "textDocument": { "uri": "file:///…/posts/a.qmd" },
  "path": "author.0.name",   // optional: a dot path, as in get-config; "" for everything
  "output": "value",          // optional: "value" (prose as markdown) or "pandoc"
  "format": "html"            // optional
}
// result
{ "uri": "…", "version": 3, "format": "html", "found": true, "value": "Ada Lovelace" }
```

`found` is `false`, with a `null` value, when `path` does not exist.

### `quarto/documentProfile`

Returns the document's profile.

```jsonc
// params
{
  "textDocument": { "uri": "file:///…/posts/a.qmd" },
  "fields": ["title", "outline"],   // optional: keep only these profile fields
  "format": "html"                  // optional
}
// result
{
  "uri": "…", "version": 3, "format": "html", "schemaVersion": 1,
  "profile": { … },     // null when the document cannot be read; see diagnostics
  "diagnostics": [ … ]  // LSP Diagnostic objects
}
```

The profile's fields:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `sourcePath` | The document's project-relative path, with `/` separators. |
| `outputHref` | Where other pages link to it, relative to the output directory. |
| `format` | The format the profile was computed for. |
| `title`, `subtitle`, `description`, `abstract` | `{ "text", "markdown" }`, or absent. |
| `authors` | Display names. `authorsStructured` has the full author model. |
| `date`, `image`, `order`, `draft`, `draftMode`, `categories`, `keywords` | As written in the metadata. |
| `outline` | Headings: `{ title, level, id, location, children }`. |
| `comments` | Editorial comments: `{ text, author, date, attributes, location }`. |
| `aliases`, `resources` | `{ value, location }`: each value as written, and where it was written. |
| `includes`, `bodyLinkTargets`, `navDependencies` | Project files: `{ path, uri }`. |
| `alwaysRender`, `engineResolution` | Render-planning information. |

A `location` is an LSP `Location`, `{ uri, range }`. A comment or heading
that comes from an included file points into that file.

### Errors

A query that cannot be answered returns `InvalidParams` (`-32602`), and
`data.kind` says why:

- `unknownDocument`: an `untitled:` document that is not open, or a URI with
  no path.
- `unsupportedInput`: not a document the server analyses, for example a config
  file or a notebook. Notebooks and scripts are not supported yet.

### Versioning

`schemaVersion` changes when the shape of a result changes in a way a client
would notice. New fields can appear without a version change.
